Here is a comprehensive summary of the study, including all key details:

---

**Title/Theme**: Multimodal Intent Understanding for Contextual Dialog Systems in Autonomous Vehicles (AVs) via AMIE — Leveraging Speech, Audio, and Visual Modalities

---

### **Core Objective**
To enhance natural human-vehicle interaction in autonomous vehicles (AVs) by developing a contextual, multimodal dialogue system — specifically, the **AMIE (Automated-vehicle Multimodal In-cabin Experience)** agent — that accurately interprets passenger commands using **three modalities**: **language/text**, **audio**, and **video** (both in-cabin and external views). The goal is to enable the AV to correctly parse user intent and trigger appropriate system actions (e.g., set destination, stop, open door, etc.). ---

### **Dataset & Data Collection**
- **Dataset**: A **multimodal in-cabin dataset** collected via a **Wizard-of-Oz scheme** using a **realistic scavenger hunt game**. - **Total utterances**: 1,331 passenger commands directed at AMIE. - **Modalities captured**:
  - **Text**: Transcribed and recognized speech (ASR output). - **Audio**: Segmented audio clips with extracted features. - **Video**: In-cabin (passenger/cabin view) and external (road view) video streams. ---

### **Key Tasks Addressed**
1. **Utterance-level intent detection** (e.g., set destination, go faster, stop, park, drop off, open door). 2. **Slot filling** (extracting contextual parameters associated with intent, e.g., location, direction, object, gesture/gaze, time, person). ---

### **Previous Work**
- Prior studies used **RNN-based models** (e.g., Bi-LSTMs) for intent detection and slot filling using **text-only** inputs. - Best-performing model: **Hierarchical & Joint Bi-LSTM (H-Joint-2)** — a two-level architecture:
  - **Level-1**: Seq2seq Bi-LSTM to detect intent keywords and slots. - **Level-2**: Joint Bi-LSTM trained on filtered keywords/slots to predict final intent. - Text features used: **GloVe word embeddings** (6B tokens, 400K vocab, dim=100). ---

### **Multimodal Features Explored**

#### 1. **Speech Embeddings (Speech2Vec)**
- Pre-trained on 500 hours of LibriSpeech. - Speech2Vec: Speech version of Word2Vec. - **Feature concatenations tested**:
  - GloVe only → F1: 0.89 (intent), 0.96 (slots)
  - GloVe + Speech2Vec → F1: 0.91 (intent), 0.97 (slots)
  - GloVe + Word2Vec + Speech2Vec → **Best performance** (F1: 0.92 intent, 0.97 slots)
- **Observation**: Speech2Vec alone underperforms GloVe due to lower vocabulary coverage, but combining it with GloVe improves results. #### 2. **Audio Features (openSMILE / IS10)**
- Extracted 1,582 features per utterance (PCM loudness, MFCC, log Mel Freq. Band, LSP, etc.). - Added to text-only and text+speech models. - **Result**: Slight improvement in intent detection (F1: 0.92). #### 3. **Visual Features (CNN-based)**
- Extracted from **Inception-ResNet-v2** (pre-trained) using 1 frame per second from segmented video clips. - **Two video sources**:
  - In-cabin (BackDriver RGB camera)
  - External (DashCam RGB camera)
- **Features**: 4,096-dim CNN activations. - **Result**: Added to text-only and text+speech models → improved intent detection to F1: 0.92. ---

### **Model Architecture**
- **H-Joint-2**: Hierarchical & Joint Bi-LSTM model. - Level-1: Extracts intent keywords and slots. - Level-2: Jointly predicts intent and refines slots using filtered keywords. - **Training**: Jointly trained for intent + slot + keyword prediction. ---

### **Experimental Results**
- **Text-only baseline**: F1 = 0.89 (intent), 0.96 (slots)
- **Text + Speech Embeddings**: F1 = 0.91 (intent), 0.97 (slots)
- **Text + Audio + Visual**: F1 = 0.92 (intent), 0.97 (slots)
- **Multimodal outperformed text-only baselines** across both intent detection and slot filling. - **Best overall performance**: **F1 = 0.92 (intent)**, **F1 = 0.97 (slot filling)**. ---

### **Key Insights & Observations**
- **Speech embeddings** significantly improve performance when combined with GloVe. - **Audio features** (paralinguistic cues) and **visual features** (gestures, gaze, external objects) provide complementary context. - **Intent types** like “stop” (audio intensity) and **slots** like “gesture/gaze” or “outside objects” remain challenging and require deeper exploration. - **Feature concatenation** is a promising approach, but further refinement is needed for specific intent/slot types. ---

### **Future Directions**
- Deepen exploration of **modality-specific features** (e.g., gaze tracking, object recognition from road view). - Improve handling of **ambiguous or complex intents** (e.g., “stop at the red light” vs.

ranked_results.content: Understanding passenger intents from spoken interactions and car's vision (both inside and outside the vehicle) are important building blocks towards developing contextual dialog systems for natural interactions in autonomous vehicles (AV). In this study, we continued exploring AMIE (Automated-vehicle Multimodal In-cabin Experience), the in-cabin agent responsible for handling certain multimodal passenger-vehicle interactions. When the passengers give instructions to AMIE, the agent should parse such commands properly considering available three modalities (language/text, audio, video) and trigger the appropriate functionality of the AV system. We had collected a multimodal in-cabin dataset with multi-turn dialogues between the passengers and AMIE using a Wizard-of-Oz scheme via realistic scavenger hunt game. In our previous explorations BIBREF0, BIBREF1, we experimented with various RNN-based models to detect utterance-level intents (set destination, change route, go faster, go slower, stop, park, pull over, drop off, open door, and others) along with intent keywords and relevant slots (location, position/direction, object, gesture/gaze, time-guidance, person) associated with the action to be performed in our AV scenarios. In this recent work, we propose to discuss the benefits of multimodal understanding of in-cabin utterances by incorporating verbal/language input (text and speech embeddings) together with the non-verbal/acoustic and visual input from inside and outside the vehicle (i.e., passenger gestures and gaze from in-cabin video stream, referred objects outside of the vehicle from the road view camera stream). Our experimental results outperformed text-only baselines and with multimodality, we achieved improved performances for utterance-level intent detection and slot filling.

ranked_results.content: Hierarchical & Joint Model (H-Joint-2): 2-level hierarchical joint learning model that detects/extracts intent keywords & slots using seq2seq Bi-LSTMs first (Level-1), then only the words that are predicted as intent keywords & valid slots are fed into Joint-2 model (Level-2), which is another seq2seq Bi-LSTM network for utterance-level intent detection (jointly trained with slots & intent keywords) BIBREF1.

ranked_results.content: Video Features: Using the feature extraction process described in BIBREF12, we extracted intermediate CNN features for each segmented video clip from AMIE dataset. For any given input video clip (segmented for each utterance), one frame per second is sampled and its visual descriptor is extracted from the activations of the intermediate convolution layers of a pre-trained CNN. We used the pre-trained Inception-ResNet-v2 model BIBREF13 and generated 4096-dim features for each sample. We experimented with adding 2 sources of visual information: (i) cabin/passenger view from the BackDriver RGB camera recordings, (ii) road/outside view from the DashCam RGB video streams.
